titleStmt.title: No. 936
Memorandum of Conversation, by the Acting Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern, South Asian, and African Affairs (Jernegan)

div.head:
No. 936
Memorandum of Conversation, by the Acting Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern, South Asian, and African Affairs (Jernegan)
div.p: Mr. Beeley came in with instructions from Mr. Eden to follow-up the talk Mr. Eden had with Secretary Dulles on December 16 on this subject. Specifically, Mr. Beeley was instructed to discuss the location, timing and “Cover plan” for the proposed Anglo-American discussions. He said it had been agreed by the two Secretaries of State in Paris that these talks should be held in early or mid-January.
I stated our views as follows:
1. Mid-January would suit us very well; we would probably not be ready to talk before that time.
2. Washington seems to us to be preferable to London as a location. It would lend itself more readily to a plausible cover story.

3. The cover story should be that Mr. Shuckburgh was coming to Washington for a general review of Middle Eastern problems with his new opposite number Assistant Secretary George Allen. This would seem very natural and it would not be noticed if Mr. Shuckburgh actually spent most of his time talking to specialists in Arab-Israel Affairs. I explained further that we were thinking of assigning Francis Russell to full-time work on this project and that he would probably have the part-time collaboration of Ambassador Raymond A. Hare. If we sent those two men, both closely identified with the Arab-Israel question, to London, it would be very likely to arouse speculation.

Mr. Beeley agreed that there seemed to be much to be said for this argument and he promised to cable it to London. He observed however that the Foreign Office might find it very difficult to spare Mr. Shuckburgh for a trip to Washington. He had already been away from his desk some seven weeks and, unlike the American Assistant Secretary, he did not have a deputy who could take over in his absence.

Since it had a direct bearing on the substance, although not the procedure, of the operation we were discussing, I gave Mr. Beeley the essence of the presentation made by Ambassador Eban of Israel in his call on Acting Secretary Hoover this afternoon. (See separate memorandum of conversation.) I pointed out that the Ambassador’s statements seemed designed to warn us against making overall peace proposals and specifically against suggesting any territorial cessions by Israel.

note.p: George V. Allen was appointed Assistant Secretary of State of Near Eastern, South Asian, and African Affairs on Jan. 24, 1955, and officially entered on duty on Jan. 26, 1955.
For Jernegan’s memorandum of Eban’s conversation with Hoover, see supra .
